陶瓷雕塑创作者 ✦ 美术史研究者 ✦ 文化遗产田野工作者: Ceramic Sculptor ✦ Art Historian ✦ Cultural Heritage Fieldworker
历史学起步，美术史研究进阶，落于陶瓷雕塑创作。常驻浙江龙泉进行艺术创作，长期从事: Trained in history, specialised in art history, and grounded in ceramic sculpture. Based in Longquan, Zhejiang; long engaged in fieldwork and cultural-heritage research, alongside ceramic restoration, kintsugi and digital modelling.
嵇鸿轩，1999 年生。本科就读历史学，硕士修读美术史研究，后于景德镇陶瓷大学攻: Born in 1999. He read History as an undergraduate, took an MA in Art History, and then studied Sculpture at Jingdezhen Ceramic University as a second bachelor, completing
的跨学科路径。 2023 年起在浙江龙泉青瓷产地创办个人工作室并常驻创作，代表作: an interdisciplinary path. Since 2023 he has kept his own studio in Longquan, Zhejiang — the historic home of celadon — with representative works including Fragrance of Steed Bones, Tile Cat, Letter from Spring, Mise (Secret Colour) and Blue Blood. Research and making run in parallel: from revolutionary-site surveys and the imagery of cake moulds to Macao funerary architecture and the handicraft community of Jingdezhen, he tends to enter a cultural site through fieldwork and iconography, and answer it in the language of clay.

从史料，到图像，再到物质——我把三种训练串成一条互相校正的链条。历史学让我习惯从: From historical sources, to images, to material — I have tied three trainings into a single chain of mutual correction. History taught me to question through primary sources and the site itself; art history taught me to read images, date them and tell the genuine from the false; sculpture forces me to return every conclusion to my hands: an idea must be formable, must survive the kiln, must be able to stand. Three degrees are not three labels stacked up, but one question tested again and again in different media.

In research I go to the site: measuring ruins, recording oral accounts, shooting material, building archives, then returning to the desk for iconographic and textual analysis. In the studio, from clay body and glaze tests to the firing curve, every step is done by hand. The revolutionary-site survey in Maoming, the Zhangtian cake moulds, the Guizhou village gazetteer, the Jingdezhen handicraft community — the field gave me the questions; the Longquan studio and the Changma cave copies gave me the ability to turn them into form.

JLPT N1 lets me work directly with Japanese sources and modern historical documents; English carries my international conference presentations; training in Latin, Sumerian and Akkadian brings far older material into view. AI-assisted qualitative research, remote-sensing archaeology and 3D modelling are the update ports I keep open for fieldwork method. Forty-odd programmes and certificates are not a collection to me — they mean every question can find a tool that fits the hand.

我的主线是学术研究，兴趣主要集中在人类学、物质文化与图像学三处。: My main line is academic research, and my interests sit chiefly in three places: anthropology, material culture and iconography.
历史学让我习惯从一手材料与现场提问，美术史让我学会读图、断代与辨伪，人类学的训练: History taught me to question through primary sources and the site itself; art history taught me to read images, date them and tell the genuine from the false; anthropology taught me to put objects, images and ritual back among the people and the everyday that produced them — not only what a thing is, but who makes it, why, and for whom. Recent work runs along three threads: funerary architectural imagery and Sino-Western visual hybridity in Macao; intangible heritage, fieldwork and oral history in western Guangdong and eastern Guizhou; and the production and identity of the Jingdezhen handicraft community — two journal articles, one master’s thesis and five conference presentations.
田野里攒下的东西，会自己找到出口，反哺到我偶尔进行的艺术创作里。: What I gather in the field finds its own way out, and feeds back into the art I make from time to time.
蹲在村子里看一场仪式、在工坊里看手艺人的手，那些形体、纹样、手势与节奏会沉下来，: Watching a ritual in a village, or a craftsman’s hands in a workshop: those forms, patterns, gestures and rhythms settle, and surface again only back in the studio — the clay and glaze of Longquan, the lines of the Changma caves, the motifs on a cake mould; the field gives them to the eye first, and the hands follow. So I make few works and do not chase output: almost every piece has a clear provenance, an extension of some survey, some oral account, some problem in an image.
